Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:131630
Court No. - 65

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 12439 of 2025
Applicant :- Putul @ Arvind Tatava

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Mahendra Ram Maurya
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Prem Shankar, Advocate holding brief of Sri Mahendra Ram Maurya, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri R.P. Patel, learned State Law Officer for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 187 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station- Dokati, District- Ballia, during the pendency of trial.

4. As per prosecution story, the marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the deceased person as per Hindu Rites on 08.06.2022, and subsequent to it, the applicant and other family members Putul @ Arvind Tatava vs State Of U.P. on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117990815/
1 are stated to have subjected the victim to cruelty for demand of dowry, thereby leading her to death on 26.10.2023.

entities.text: Putul @ Arvind Tatava vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
It is further argued that P.W.1, the informant has been examined and he has not supported the prosecution story although he had not been declared hostile.
There is no likelihood of conviction of applicant in the case.
6. It is further argued by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no criminal antecedent of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 28.10.2023 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Learned State Law Officer has vehemently opposed the bail application.
8. This Court had called for the report regarding status of trial and as per status report dated 28.07.2025, two witnesses have been examined and the date is fixed for cross-examination of P.W.-2.
9. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

10. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
11.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
12. Learned State Law Officer could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
13. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned State Law Officer.

14. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the fact that P.W.-1, the informant Putul @ Arvind Tatava vs State Of U.P. on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117990815/
2 has not supported the prosecution story and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Putul @ Arvind Tatava vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant- Putul @ Arvind Tatava, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence during trial.
(ii) The applicant shall not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed.
16. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

17. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

Order Date :- 5.8.2025 Karan (Justice Krishan Pahal)
